layers.process: Visitors can't stay on Rapa Nui (Easter Island) for more than 30 consecutive days.

layers.authority: Ministerio del Interior y Seguridad Pública de Chile; checked by the PDI (Policía de Investigaciones)
layers.process: Every tourist or invited guest completes the free Formulario Único de Ingreso (FUI, single entry form) online at ingresorapanui.interior.gob.cl before travel and shows it to the PDI at the departure airport or port; without it you can't board. Tourists need an ID or passport, a non-transferable return ticket dated no more than 30 days after arrival, and a booking at accommodation authorised by Sernatur (the national tourism service), or a letter of invitation from a Rapa Nui person or other authorised resident with a folio number from the Gobernación Provincial de Isla de Pascua. Rapa Nui people registered with CONADI, and people authorised under Law 21.070, show only their ID.

laws.rule: Entering Rapa Nui National Park requires a personal park ticket for each visitor and an accredited guide (Ma'u Henua). Rano Raraku and Orongo can be visited only once per ticket.
laws.heading: Park entry requirements; Park rules

laws.rule: Park rules: keep the permitted distance from moai and ahu without touching or leaning on them; do not move or remove stones or archaeological objects; stay on marked trails; no graffiti; no fires or camping; no pets; no drones without authorisation; no alcohol or smoking in the park; no commercial filming without permission.
laws.heading: Park rules

laws.rule: The ticket is personal and non-transferable and is valid for 10 days; carry it with your ID card or passport at the sites.

sites.what: Moai and ahu across the park, including Rano Raraku and Orongo; Kāiŋa ʻOno Tupuna, sacred land of the Rapa Nui people, a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1995) and National Monument (Law 17.288) managed by the Ma'u Henua Indigenous Community.
